newsitem.title: USA: Excel, Telco in $1.2 billion merger deal.
newsitem.headline: Excel, Telco in $1.2 billion merger deal.

text.p: Excel Communications Inc. said early Friday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Telco Communications Group Inc. for about $1.2 billion.

The deal would create a combined company with consolidated revenues of $2 billion and 11 billion long distance minutes of usage on an annualized basis, 6.3 million customers, and 100,000 network miles of DS-3 fiber optic capacity, it said.
Under the terms of the agreement, all shareholders of Telco will receive 0.7595 shares of common stock of the combined company and $15 in cash for each share of Telco common stock.
All shareholders of Excel will receive one share of common stock of the combined company for each share of Excel common stock.
Upon completion of the merger, Excel shareholders will own about 80 percent of the combined company. The transaction will be accounted for as a purchase, it said.

Excel also said it obtained a $1 billion committed line of credit from an affiliate of Lehman Brothers, of which an estimated $500 million to $600 million will be used to fund the cash portion of the merger and to refinance the existing indebtedness of Telco.
The merger agreement has been unanimously approved by the board of directors of each company.
At the merger's closing Telco Group will keep its headquarters in Chantilly, Virginia, and its current management team will continue to operate it.
Excel said it estimates it can realise cost savings in excess of $100 million in the first full fiscal year after the merger is closed.
